manual: Experimental Instruction Manual: Touching a Hot Object Causes Rapid Hand WithdrawalI. Basic Experiment Information1. Experiment Title: Touching a Hot Object Causes Rapid Hand Withdrawal2. Subject: Natural Science - Biology3. Experiment Objective: To demonstrate that touching a hot object triggers a rapid withdrawal response, and to understand the protective reflex mechanism of the human nervous system.II. Experimental MaterialsVisibly hot metal surface (e.g., heated metal plate or metal rod under safe supervision), human hand (demonstrator), heat source (for preheating metal, not shown in core demonstration), safety supervision.III. Experimental Procedure1. Preparation: Ensure the metal surface is visibly hot (e.g., slight heat shimmer or warning indicator). The demonstrator positions their hand near the metal.2. Core Operation: The person briefly touches the hot metal surface with their hand.3. Immediate Response: Upon contact, the person quickly withdraws their hand from the metal surface.4. Completion: The hand remains away from the hot surface after withdrawal.IV. Observation of Experimental Phenomena1. Before contact: The metal surface appears hot; the hand is stationary near it.2. During contact: The hand briefly touches the metal surface.3. After contact: The hand is rapidly pulled away, showing a quick and involuntary response.V. Summary of Experimental PrincipleThis experiment demonstrates a protective reflex. Heat stimulates pain receptors in the skin, generating nerve impulses that travel to the spinal cord. The spinal cord immediately sends motor signals to muscles in the arm, causing rapid withdrawal before conscious awareness. This reflex helps prevent serious burns and tissue damage.
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target concept: Human protective reflex to harmful heat. Minimum assumptions: the metal surface is hot enough to stimulate pain receptors, and the person has a normal nervous system. Expected phased storyline: (1) visible hot metal and approaching hand; (2) brief contact acting as heat stimulus; (3) rapid withdrawal as an effect of the reflex arc. The causal transition from heat contact to withdrawal must be visually clear, continuous, and observable within a short time window, with the hand and metal surface always in view for verification.
